requirement:
The coverage check MUST fail when no usable coverage has been collected, or when
a selected latest attempt has missing, unreadable, or stale coverage. It MUST
distinguish these measurement failures from measured lines with zero execution
and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage. Exception
evidence MUST NOT excuse measurement failures or permit substitution of an
older attempt. Excluded historical runs and incompatible configurations MUST
NOT by themselves cause failure.

Coverage whose format does not support the function attribution required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` MUST be rejected with guidance
to recollect coverage. When missing or corrupt metadata prevents establishing
the latest-per-test selection or active configuration, the check MUST fail
rather than silently use remaining records. Historical data MAY be disregarded
without failure only when its exclusion can be established.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. All of them are in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`. I read the implementation only to confirm how the active configuration is chosen (the configuration of the last record in `book.rs#fn[load_saved]`) and which diagnostics `check_saved` emits.

Obligations mapped to tests:

- **No usable coverage must fail.**
  - `stale_missing_legacy_and_uncertain_history_cannot_use_older_success` asserts that `report` does not pass on a project with no records.
  - `accepted_exceptions_cannot_waive_invalid_measurement_and_checks_still_collect_errors` covers the "absent" case and the "empty lines" case, which expects "No usable instrumented lines".
- **A selected latest attempt with missing, unreadable or stale coverage must fail, and an older success must not be substituted.**
  - In the stale/missing/legacy test, an older passing attempt exists. The newer attempt then has its profile removed, which expects "missing or unreadable". A later attempt is made stale by editing the source, which expects "stale coverage".
  - The accepted-exceptions test repeats the missing-profile and stale cases, each after an older good attempt, and asserts failure.
- **Measurement failures must be distinguished from zero-execution lines and from functions absent from usable coverage.**
  - In `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, `#fn[a]: zero execution` and `#fn[a]: not measured` appear as separate findings.
  - In `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear`, `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` and `#fn[missing]: not measured` appear as separate findings.
  - Measurement failures use different texts: "missing or unreadable", "stale coverage", "lacks function attribution", "corrupt function attribution" and "No usable instrumented lines".
  - The accepted-exceptions test also asserts that the zero-execution text `0/1 (0.0%)` is absent from failure output.
- **Exception evidence must not excuse measurement failures.** `accepted_exceptions_cannot_waive_invalid_measurement_and_checks_still_collect_errors` gives the file and function accepted citations, then runs absent, missing profile, legacy, corrupt counters, stale, corrupt history and empty lines. Each case must fail with no "accepted exception" text.
- **Excluded historical runs and incompatible configurations must not cause failure.**
  - The stale/missing/legacy test records an older `other-config` attempt with `functions = None`. The report still passes.
  - After a good attempt 5 supersedes earlier broken attempts of the same test (missing profile, legacy, stale), the report passes again.
- **Unsupported function attribution must be rejected with guidance.** The legacy case with `functions = None` expects "lacks function attribution" and "recollect coverage with this Habeas version".
- **Missing or corrupt metadata must fail rather than fall back to remaining records.** A corrupt `run.json` expects "cannot establish latest-per-test". This is checked in both the stale/missing/legacy test and the accepted-exceptions "corrupt history" case.
- **The "MAY be disregarded" clause for historical data** imposes nothing to test.

The `{test}` references on these functions are present. `readable_failed_execution_can_contribute_but_outcomes_remain_visible` adds that a failed outcome with readable coverage still passes, and that a process diagnostic makes the check fail.

I found no missing scenario that the requirement text names.

text: :::{req} check.measurement
The coverage check MUST fail when no usable coverage has been collected, or when
a selected latest attempt has missing, unreadable, or stale coverage. It MUST
distinguish these measurement failures from measured lines with zero execution
and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage. Exception
evidence MUST NOT excuse measurement failures or permit substitution of an
older attempt. Excluded historical runs and incompatible configurations MUST
NOT by themselves cause failure.
Coverage whose format does not support the function attribution required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` MUST be rejected with guidance
to recollect coverage. When missing or corrupt metadata prevents establishing
the latest-per-test selection or active configuration, the check MUST fail
rather than silently use remaining records. Historical data MAY be disregarded
without failure only when its exclusion can be established.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
